measured: Four producer-native messages normalise onto four envelopes that reproduce entries/{human,event,schedule,external}.json exactly, byte for byte through the canonical form (test.sh step 1).
One job digest and one resolved manifest across the four doors, against four entry ids, four correlation ids, four executing identities and four derived keys (step 1).
All four entry documents validate against examples/end-to-end/schemas/entry.schema.json with that example's own validator, 0 errors (step 1).
Every ledger record carries run id, correlation id, attested subject, entry id, key, and a non-blank executing and triggering identity - on refusals as well as admissions (steps 1, 9).
No producer body carries an idempotency key, a correlation id, a run id or a ceiling; the key the boundary derives equals the key each entry document declares, at all four doors (step 2).
An identity a producer claimed for itself (claimed_submitter, submittedBy) never reaches an envelope; the attested subject stands (step 2).
Every producer-specific attribute is named in the receipt's dropped list, computed from what the mapper declares it reads (step 2).
Every member of every dropped list is named in README's 'Carried and not consumed' table, checked from the receipts to the table and not only from the table to the receipts (step 2).

DIFFERENTIAL parent_correlation_fields: with contextId named, the external entry carries the partner's context as parent_correlation_id at depth 1; with the row removed the same message has no parent and depth 0, and this run's own correlation id is unchanged (step 2).
The budget ceiling on all four envelopes is the one admission.json stamps, and no producer supplied it (step 2).
A replay under the same derived key returns the stored acknowledgement, keeps the original correlation id, and records nothing new (step 3).
The same key with a different job is refused 409 idempotency-conflict and the second job is never admitted (step 3).

DIFFERENTIAL key_fields: a catch-up delivery of one schedule occurrence is one key and one entry under the declared derivation, and two keys and two entries when the declaration names the wall clock (step 3).
The next nominal occurrence of the same schedule derives a different key (step 3).

DIFFERENTIAL idempotency binding: with the read/write window widened, 8 concurrent redeliveries are answered fresh 8 times by the fold binding and once by the lease binding, and the two declare different units of conditionality (step 4).
A malformed envelope is refused 422 with a located violation - instance location /occurred_at and its keyword location - and both validator implementations rejected it; nothing recorded (step 5).
DIFFERENTIAL dialect: against a schema declaring another dialect, the same valid envelope is refused 422 dialect-unsupported before any instance is checked (step 5).
DIFFERENTIAL validation binding: walk-per-document against compile-once, schema_reads 2 against 0, same dialect and same envelope (step 5).

Delegation depth 1, 2, 2, 3 at the four doors; the triggering identity is present at every one; and within one chain, each hop's issued scope is a strict subset of the hop before it and its lifetime strictly shorter - read per hop off the record, not by comparing two doors (step 6).

DIFFERENTIAL identity.scopes: with four rungs the external door's three hops hold three distinct narrowing scopes; with two rungs the same chain is refused 403 scope-ladder-shorter-than-chain, no credential issued and nothing recorded (step 6).
DIFFERENTIAL max_delegation_depth: the external door's three hops are admitted at 4 and refused 403 delegation-depth-bound at 2, with nothing recorded (step 6).
DIFFERENTIAL identity binding: authority calls 3 against 0 for the same issued chain (step 6).
An allow names the rule that fired and the digest of the rule set it was pinned to (step 7).
DIFFERENTIAL tenant: a resource in another tenant is refused 403 with spend_delta_micros 0 and no entry (step 7).

DIFFERENTIAL policy.action: under the declared vocabulary submit is allowed by allow-entry-in-tenant; an action the vocabulary does not name is refused 403 deny-entry-action-outside-vocabulary with spend_delta_micros 0 and no entry, under the same pinned version; the same action is allowed once actions_permitted names it, and the pin moves with the vocabulary (step 7).
DIFFERENTIAL policy binding: two engines return the same effect, rule id and pinned version (step 7).
DIFFERENTIAL ceiling: 1500000 admits with positive headroom, 1000 refuses 402 before a claim is taken and before anything is recorded (step 8).
DIFFERENTIAL producers: the registered formats admit, an unregistered one is refused 403 refuse-unmapped-producer naming the registered set, and the refusal names who was at the door (step 9).

DIFFERENTIAL intake binding: a detached submission produces the same job digest with a different acknowledgement delivery, no producer present at the acknowledgement, and one more hop on the chain, and that fourth hop is issued the fourth rung of the declared ladder - 600s and one scope - rather than a repeat of the third (step 9).
The capability description names four doors, the schema, the dialect, the lifecycle states and the retention window, all read from the declaration (step 10).
The failure modes the description advertises are exactly the six this run produced - not a longer list and not a shorter one (step 12).
DIFFERENTIAL lifecycle: cancellable is true in the description and on the receipt with cancelled declared, and false without it (step 10).
The receipt chain verifies; a one-character edit is detected; two runs of the four doors are byte-identical (step 11).
An unreachable recording path is refused 503 retryable, the claim taken for it is released, and no entry is written (step 11).
No product name appears in any of the 12 files of this example except README.md, this example's test.sh among them, matched word-anchored against 25 names (step 12).
provenance.cites is exactly the set of record ids the example's rows carry, in either direction (step 12).
claimed: Durability. The claim store, the intake binding's replay map and the entry record all live in one process, so replay, conflict and the lease race are measured between threads and claimed for a second process, a restart, or the declared retention window (gap 3).

Revocation. Credentials are issued short-lived by a dry-run binding against a fixture the adapter itself produced; nothing is verified against a live issuer, no audience is discovered from a resource, and nothing is withdrawn mid-flight, so 'revocable while work is in flight' is claimed (gap 7).
Conformance of the validators. Their agreement is measured on five documents; the published language-agnostic conformance suite is not run against either (gap 1).
Provenance. The receipt is hash-chained by a ledger this repository wrote; no outside verifier can check an admission (gap 4).
Subscription and cancellation. The description advertises the declared lifecycle; no subscription, streaming or cancellation operation exists in this example (gap 5).

Producer-identity uniqueness. The derivation trusts that a producer's declared identity members are unique per message, which the event envelope standard obliges the producer to guarantee and nothing here checks (gap 8).
Per-schedule and per-subscription registration. authorised_by is declared per producer format, not per named schedule or subscription (gap 6).
The held-out check. This area has a visible check and no hidden one, so by build-example's own rule it is incomplete rather than passing (gap 9).

Registry agreement. Six problem types are produced and advertised, but no check reconciles the intake, validation and idempotency capabilities' local registries with the platform's ten-row closed registry, and dialect-unsupported has a row in none of them (gap 2).
